context: Evaluates whether the agent correctly treats a hook-invoked CLI binary as an active tool rather than concluding it is inactive because it is absent from .mcp.json, then correctly reports its watch/dormant status as a staleness note rather than a removal finding. Covers Workflow steps 2-4 and the hook-wiring anti-pattern.

checklist.name: Tool identified as active
checklist.description: The response states that lintguard is active, based on the hook command

checklist.name: mcp.json absence not treated as proof of inactivity
checklist.description: The response does not conclude not installed or inactive from .mcp.json absence alone

checklist.name: Hook checked as well as MCP registration
checklist.description: The response makes clear both MCP-server registration and hook wiring were checked, not just one

checklist.name: Binary path mapped to dataset id
checklist.description: The hook's binary path is connected to the dataset entry for lintguard using judgement, not exact string matching

checklist.name: Watch plus dormant reported as staleness note
checklist.description: The watch decision with dormant activityStatus is reported as a staleness note

checklist.name: Not treated as a removal finding
checklist.description: The staleness signal alone is not used to recommend removing the hook

checklist.name: User's literal question answered
checklist.description: The response directly answers whether lintguard is in use, not just the staleness note

checklist.name: No silent hook edit
checklist.description: The hook command in settings.json is not edited or removed by the agent in this turn
